metadata.title: Implement Log Parser with Parquet Caching

story.soThat: comparison operations run quickly on large log files

tasks.task: Create log_parser.py module Create rustybt/validation/log_parser.py Define parse_log() function signature Implement JSONL line-by-line parsing Convert to Polars DataFrame
Implement Parquet caching Check for existing cache file Compare mtime of JSONL vs Parquet Read from cache if valid Write to cache after parsing Support use_cache=False bypass
Implement flatten_data_column() Detect nested "data" dict column Extract keys and create prefixed columns Handle missing keys with nulls Preserve non-nested columns
Add schema validation Define required fields list Validate each record on parse Collect and report errors with line numbers Raise clear exception for invalid logs
Optimize for performance Use streaming read for large files Benchmark with 100MB test file Profile and optimize bottlenecks if needed
Write unit tests Test basic JSONL parsing Test Parquet cache creation Test cache invalidation on source change Test flatten_data_column() Test schema validation errors Test use_cache=False

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: parse_log() function implemented in rustybt/validation/log_parser.py - accepts log_path: Path, use_cache: bool = True, returns pl.DataFrame
Parquet caching works correctly - cache regenerated if JSONL newer, skipped if use_cache=False
flatten_data_column() expands nested JSON with "data_" prefix
Performance meets target - parse 100MB JSONL in less than 5 seconds
Log schema validation - required fields timestamp, layer, event; clear error messages

doc.title: Architecture - Log-Based Validation
doc.snippet: JSONL primary format for human readability, Parquet caching for performance, Polars DataFrame for analysis. Log schema defines timestamp, layer, event, asset, data fields.

doc.title: Architecture - Performance Considerations
doc.snippet: Log parsing target: less than 5 seconds per 100MB JSONL. Parquet caching provides 10-100x faster queries. Stream large files to manage memory.

doc.title: PRD - Test Suite Development
doc.snippet: System can ingest structured logs from both rustybt and Backtrader. System can parse logs into standardized data structures for comparison.

doc.title: Epic 4 - Story 4.1 Specification
doc.section: Story 4.1: Implement Log Parser with Parquet Caching
doc.snippet: Parse JSONL log file to Polars DataFrame with optional Parquet caching. Cache invalidation based on mtime comparison. Flatten nested data column.

constraints.constraint: Log schema: timestamp (required), layer (required), event (required), asset (optional), data (optional dict)
JSONL format for human readability, Parquet for performance caching
Stream large files - don't load entirely into memory
Prefix flattened columns with "data_" for clarity
NFR22: Log parsing must handle large log files efficiently (>100MB logs)
NFR5: Test results must be deterministic (same inputs always produce same results)
